title: Ethics & Relationships: Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the key terms for marriage, family and relationships in Christianity and Islam.
meta_desc: GCSE RS Relationships foundations — marriage, family, cohabitation and key vocabulary.
final_note: You now know the foundational vocabulary for ethics and relationships.

concepts.def: A legally or religiously recognised union; many Christians see it as a lifelong covenant before God for companionship, support and raising children.
Living together as a couple without being married; accepted by many today but discouraged by some religious traditions.
A sexual relationship with someone other than one's spouse, condemned in the Ten Commandments and regarded as a serious wrong in most religions.
The legal ending of a marriage; religions differ, with Catholic teaching rejecting divorce while Islam permits it as a last resort.
Methods of preventing pregnancy; Catholic teaching opposes artificial contraception, while most Protestant churches permit it within marriage.
Religious traditions stress duties within the family: parents nurture and educate children in faith, and children honour their parents.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Christian marriage is a lifelong covenant — 'What God has joined together, let no one separate' (Mark 10:9).

Purposes: love, faithfulness, procreation, mutual support.

Catholics regard marriage as a sacrament; most Protestants see it as a sacred covenant rather than a sacrament.

In Islam marriage (nikah) is a contract before Allah and witnesses, strongly encouraged for adult Muslims.

The Qur'an describes spouses as 'garments for one another' (2:187).

Faithfulness and family life are central duties.

Family types include nuclear, extended, single-parent, same-sex and blended families.

Christianity traditionally teaches parents should raise children in faith (Proverbs 22:6). Islam teaches strong respect for parents — 'Lower the wing of humility' to them (Qur'an 17:24).

mcqs.q: What is the difference between annulment and divorce in Catholic teaching?
options: An annulment is a blessing given on a wedding anniversary.
An annulment declares a sacramental marriage was never valid in the first place; divorce claims to end a valid marriage, which the Catholic Church does not recognise.
Contraception is mentioned in the Ten Commandments.
Annulment is simply the Catholic word for divorce.
Muslim divorce requires the approval of a Christian court.
Divorce is absolutely forbidden for Muslims in all circumstances.
An annulment is a blessing given on a wedding anniversary.
No — divorce is permitted in Islam as a last resort after attempts at reconciliation, followed by a waiting period (iddah), though hadith describes it as disliked by Allah.

mcqs.q: Do all Christians hold the same view on contraception?
options: An annulment is a blessing given on a wedding anniversary.
Contraception is mentioned in the Ten Commandments.
All Christians are forbidden from using any form of contraception.
No — official Catholic teaching opposes artificial contraception (Humanae Vitae, 1968), while most Protestant churches accept it as a responsible choice within marriage.
